title: Maximum Diagonal Sum by Ring Rotations
description:
You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `matrix`. Before computing the sum of its two main diagonals, you may independently rotate **each concentric square ring** of `matrix` clockwise by any non-negative number of positions (rotating a ring shifts only the perimeter cells of that ring along its cyclic boundary).

Return the **maximum possible sum** of all cells lying on the primary diagonal (`r == c`) or the secondary diagonal (`r + c == n - 1`), counting the center cell once when `n` is odd.
hints: Concentric rings can be rotated completely independently, and each ring k of side length L = n - 2k >= 2 contributes exactly its 4 corner cells to the two diagonals.

In cyclic order around ring k, the 4 corner slots are spaced S = L - 1 positions apart, so any rotation places the quadruple {(k, k+i), (k+i, k+S), (k+S, k+S-i), (k+S-i, k)} onto the corners for some 0 <= i < S.

examples.explanation: Rotating the outer 3x3 ring by 1 step moves the four edge midpoints (10, 10, 10, 10) onto the four corners; adding the center cell 5 gives 45.
In a 2x2 matrix, all four cells always lie on the diagonals regardless of rotation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
In a 4x4 matrix, outer ring picks the best of 3 phases and inner 2x2 ring always contributes all 4 of its cells.
